name: CircuitBreaker / BreakerHandle

test_list.description: N failures inside the window move Closed to Open { until: now + cooldown }; N-1 failures leave it Closed.
Failures older than the window no longer count: spaced-out failures never open the breaker.
While Open and before the cooldown elapsed, allow() is false.
The first allow() at or after the cooldown moves Open to HalfOpen and admits exactly that one probe; a second caller is refused while the probe is in flight.
A successful probe closes the breaker and clears the failure history.
A failed probe reopens the breaker for a fresh cooldown.
on_success / on_failure reported while Open (results of calls admitted before the trip) do not change the state or extend the cooldown.
BreakerHandle publishes exactly one CircuitTripped event when the breaker opens (not for later failures while Open) and shows up in the supervisor snapshot.
With tokio paused time: open, advance past the cooldown, exactly one probe is admitted, and its success closes the breaker.
For any operation sequence the observed state never goes Closed -> HalfOpen directly.
The breaker agrees with an independent reference model on every allow() answer and every state, for any sequence of allow / success / failure at non-decreasing times.

inputs.name: max_failures
inputs.description: Failures inside the window that open the breaker.

inputs.name: window
inputs.description: Sliding window in which failures count.

inputs.name: cooldown
inputs.description: How long the breaker stays Open before one probe is admitted.

inputs.name: now
inputs.description: Injected time; the state machine never reads a clock.

output_description: Closed, Open { until } or HalfOpen; allow() answers whether the caller may proceed.
